references.text: The sin offering with a male goat to make atonement is a recurring theme in Leviticus, where the male goat is used to make atonement for sin.
On the Day of Atonement, a male goat was slaughtered as a sin offering to make atonement for the people, which parallels the use of the male goat in Numbers 28:30.
A male goat as a sin offering to make atonement is also mentioned here as part of the sacrificial regulations.
Earlier in the same chapter, the male goat is mentioned as a sin offering during the new moon sacrifice, with the same purpose of making atonement.
During the Passover festival, a male goat is also offered as a sin offering to make atonement, which is identical in purpose to verse 30.
At the New Year festival, a male goat is offered as a sin offering to make atonement, following the same pattern as in 28:30.

The book of Hebrews explains how Christ entered the holy place with his own blood to obtain eternal redemption, in contrast to the blood of goats and calves. This shows the fulfillment of the atoning sacrifice in the Old Testament.
The book of Hebrews states that the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins, pointing to the need for Christ's perfect offering as a substitute for the Old Testament atoning sacrifices.
